title: Creating a site never invalidates sitesAccessCache, so the creator is 403 Forbidden on that site for up to 15 seconds (issue #980, closed as completed, is not fixed)
statement: POST /organizations/:organizationId/sites returns 201, but the per-user sites-access cache that every site-scoped authorization check reads is not invalidated, so for up to its 15 second TTL the creator's own follow-up calls on the new site answer 403 Forbidden. The API docs promise a key tied to the user account grants access to all sites in the organization, and the identical request succeeds unchanged after 16 seconds. Upstream #980 was closed 'completed' on 2026-05-22 with 'Will be fixed in the next version!', and the fix is still absent.

handVerified.note: Report section 1. Both cache keys carry the defect. `${userId}:false` (goals, funnels, GET /sites/:id/excluded-*): site created, immediate POST /api/sites/5/goals -> 403, same call after 16 s idle -> 201. A PUT /config on a new site at +16121 ms succeeded and the GET /api/sites/7/excluded-paths of that same write at +16125 ms was 403, four milliseconds apart, same cookie, same site. `${userId}:true` (PUT /config) needed a second, non-system-admin account because requireSiteAdminAccess short-circuits for better-auth system admins before touching the cache, and the first user in a fresh database is auto-promoted (auth.ts:358-360); with that account, PUT /api/sites/9/config -> 403 then 200 after 16 s. The report also corrects run-classification.md rows 9 and 10: the failing request in those two scenarios is the excluded-* GET at step 3, not the PUT at step 2, which succeeds. Ten board scenarios red on this.

source.howDecided: git log 613cd015..HEAD on all four files returns nothing: not one of the four commits since the tested commit touches them. At HEAD the cache is still auth-utils.ts:122-126 (NodeCache, stdTTL 15), invalidateSitesAccessCache is still auth-utils.ts:297-300, and grep -rn over server/src (tests excluded) lists exactly eight call sites, byte-identical to the tested commit: auth.ts:180, auth.ts:566, auth.ts:589, memberAccess/updateMemberSiteAccess.ts:86, sites/applySiteMove.ts:35, teams/createTeam.ts:97, teams/updateTeam.ts:114, teams/deleteTeam.ts:38. server/src/api/sites/addSite.ts, the handler behind POST /organizations/:organizationId/sites, still neither imports nor calls it.

reevaluation: The finding stands unchanged and the report's upstream claim is exactly right: #980 is closed as completed and the behaviour it describes is still in master today. Nothing moved on the issue since 2026-05-22, no PR references the creation path, and the culprit files have had zero commits since the tested commit. Worth knowing for the follow-up: the only auth-utils.ts change anywhere near the close date is 672a65c5 (2026-05-21, 'Enhance funnel and goal deletion logic with site ID validation'), which lands the day before the close and adds site-id validation to deleteFunnel, deleteGoal and updateGoal plus formatting churn in getSitesUserHasAccessTo. It adds no invalidation on any creation path, which is the most likely explanation for a good-faith close that did not fix the reported symptom. The latest release tag is v2.8.0 (2026-07-26), which is an ancestor of the tested commit, so the shipped release carries the defect too, and the tested commit itself is in no tag. Scope and severity are if anything wider than #980 records: the reporter saw it only on POST /goal and POST /funnel, whereas the defect covers every route behind requireSiteAccess (including the GET /sites/:id/excluded-* family) and, for any org owner who is not a better-auth system admin, every route behind requireSiteAdminAccess. The failure direction is fail-closed (a legitimate user is denied), so this is a correctness and usability defect on an authorization path, not a privilege escalation, and it does not need a security channel.

ROUTE DETAIL, read this first. Do not open a fresh issue: reopen the conversation on #980 by commenting there. Our filing account is an outside contributor and cannot reopen an issue closed by someone else, so the comment has to give a maintainer everything needed to reopen it themselves. Include, in this order: (1) the one-line claim that #980 is not fixed in master at 64f8c4fb7f394bdfe9379717de8e6c21758b1ac2; (2) the root cause with permalinks, that addSite.ts never calls invalidateSitesAccessCache while eight other paths do, and the cache at auth-utils.ts:122-126 has stdTTL 15; (3) the timed repro and its control, create a site then POST /api/sites/<new>/goals immediately -> 403, idle 16 s -> 201, nothing else changed; (4) the four-millisecond pair, PUT /api/sites/<new>/config -> 200 at +16121 ms, GET /api/sites/<new>/excluded-paths -> 403 at +16125 ms, which is the sharpest single piece of evidence because write and read of the same site disagree in the same breath; (5) the two independently-keyed halves, and that a better-auth system admin (the first user in a fresh database, auth.ts:358-360) can never observe the `${userId}:true` half, which is a plausible reason an internal check looked green; (6) that the reporter's own symptom set is a subset, since the whole requireSiteAccess surface is affected. Do not speculate about what the 'next version' fix was; say only that no commit on the creation path exists and cite 672a65c5 as the nearest change, phrased as a question rather than an accusation. Keep the tone of someone continuing a thread, not filing a complaint.
